meta.title: Very Advanced Pro English (C1 and C2) Assessment

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Inversion] -> Negative adverbs like 'Rarely' at the beginning of a sentence trigger subject-auxiliary inversion. The base form of the verb must follow the auxiliary 'did'. | [Topik: Inversi] Kata keterangan negatif seperti 'Rarely' di awal kalimat memicu inversi subjek-auksiliaris. Bentuk dasar kata kerja harus mengikuti auksiliaris 'did'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Subjunctive Mood] -> Verbs and adjectives expressing urgency (e.g., imperative, essential) require the base form of the verb (subjunctive) in the 'that' clause, regardless of the subject. | [Topik: Subjungtif] Kata kerja dan kata sifat yang mendesak (misalnya, imperative, essential) mengharuskan penggunaan bentuk dasar kata kerja (subjungtif) dalam klausa 'that', terlepas dari subjeknya.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Mixed Conditionals] -> This sentence correctly uses a mixed conditional to describe a past action with a present result. 'Had accepted' (past perfect) pairs with 'would be living' (present conditional). | [Topik: Pengandaian Campuran] Kalimat ini dengan benar menggunakan pengandaian campuran untuk menggambarkan tindakan masa lalu dengan hasil di masa kini.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Participle Clauses] -> 'Being completed' implies a passive ongoing action, which doesn't fit the context of the team celebrating. The perfect active participle 'Having completed' shows the action was finished before the main verb. | [Topik: Klausa Partisip] 'Being completed' menyiratkan tindakan pasif yang sedang berlangsung. Partisip sempurna aktif 'Having completed' menunjukkan tindakan selesai sebelum kata kerja utama.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Prepositional Phrases] -> The correct formal phrase is 'by virtue of', meaning 'because of' or 'as a result of'. 'For' is incorrect here. | [Topik: Frasa Preposisional] Frasa formal yang benar adalah 'by virtue of', yang berarti 'karena' atau 'sebagai hasil dari'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Relative Pronouns] -> 'Whose' is the correct relative pronoun to indicate possession (the members of the board). 'Which' cannot be used to show possession in this way. | [Topik: Kata Ganti Penghubung] 'Whose' adalah kata ganti penghubung yang benar untuk menunjukkan kepemilikan.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Future in the Past] -> The structure 'was/were to have + past participle' is used to talk about something that was planned but did not happen. 'Had' is grammatically incorrect here. | [Topik: Masa Depan dalam Masa Lalu] Struktur 'was/were to have + past participle' digunakan untuk membicarakan sesuatu yang direncanakan tetapi tidak terjadi.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Subjunctive 'Wish'] -> When expressing regret about a past event using 'wish', we use the Past Perfect tense ('had + past participle'), not 'would have'. | [Topik: Subjungtif 'Wish'] Saat mengungkapkan penyesalan tentang peristiwa masa lalu dengan 'wish', kita menggunakan Past Perfect ('had + past participle').

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Dangling Modifiers / Absolute Phrases] -> The participle phrase must logically connect to the sentence. Adding 'It' creates a correct absolute phrase ('It being a nice day...'). | [Topik: Penggantung Modifikasi] Menambahkan 'It' menciptakan frasa absolut yang benar ('It being a nice day...').

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Parallel Structure] -> Items in a list must be in the same grammatical form. Since 'to increase' and 'to expand' are infinitives, 'improving' must be changed to the infinitive 'to improve'. | [Topik: Struktur Paralel] Item dalam daftar harus memiliki bentuk tata bahasa yang sama.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Gerunds vs. Infinitives] -> 'Stop + gerund' means to quit an action entirely. 'Stop + infinitive' means to pause one action in order to do another. The context implies quitting the habit, so 'smoking' is correct. | [Topik: Gerund vs Infinitif] 'Stop + gerund' berarti berhenti melakukan suatu tindakan.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Conjunctions] -> 'Albeit' means 'although' but is typically followed by an adjective, adverb, or prepositional phrase, not a full clause with a subject and verb. 'Although' is required here. | [Topik: Konjungsi] 'Albeit' biasanya diikuti oleh kata sifat atau frasa, bukan klausa penuh.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Passive Reporting Verbs] -> The passive structure for reporting verbs is 'Subject + is/are + past participle + to-infinitive'. 'Believing' is active and incorrect. | [Topik: Kata Kerja Pelaporan Pasif] Struktur pasif untuk kata kerja pelaporan adalah 'Subjek + is/are + past participle + to-infinitive'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement] -> With 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Employees' is plural, so the verb must be 'were'. | [Topik: Kesesuaian Subjek-Kata Kerja] Dengan 'neither... nor', kata kerja menyesuaikan dengan subjek yang paling dekat ('employees' adalah jamak).

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Noun Clauses as Subjects] -> A noun clause acting as the subject of a sentence generally takes a singular verb. 'What I find most troubling' is a singular concept, requiring 'is'. | [Topik: Klausa Kata Benda sebagai Subjek] Klausa kata benda yang bertindak sebagai subjek kalimat umumnya menggunakan kata kerja tunggal.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Future Perfect Continuous] -> The correct structure is 'will have been + verb-ing'. 'Will be having been' is grammatically invalid and overly complex. | [Topik: Future Perfect Continuous] Struktur yang benar adalah 'will have been + verb-ing'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Modals of Deduction] -> To express a logical conclusion about a past event, use 'must have + past participle'. 'Must been' is missing the auxiliary 'have'. | [Topik: Modus Deduksi] Untuk menyatakan kesimpulan logis tentang peristiwa masa lalu, gunakan 'must have + past participle'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Phrasal Verbs] -> The correct phrasal verb meaning 'to abolish' or 'to eliminate' is 'do away with'. 'For' is the wrong preposition. | [Topik: Frasa Kerja] Frasa kerja yang benar yang berarti 'menghapuskan' adalah 'do away with'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Quantifiers and Uncountable Nouns] -> 'Research' is an uncountable noun. 'A great deal of' is a singular quantifier phrase, so it requires the singular verb 'has been'. | [Topik: Kata Bilangan dan Kata Benda Tak Bisa Dihitung] 'Research' adalah kata benda tak bisa dihitung dan membutuhkan kata kerja tunggal 'has been'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Uncountable Nouns and Articles] -> 'Information' is an uncountable noun and cannot be preceded by the indefinite article 'an'. | [Topik: Kata Benda Tak Bisa Dihitung dan Artikel] 'Information' adalah kata benda tak bisa dihitung dan tidak dapat didahului oleh artikel tak tentu 'an'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Verb Patterns] -> The verb 'deny' is followed by a gerund (verb-ing), not an infinitive. 'Having stolen' or 'stealing' is correct. | [Topik: Pola Kata Kerja] Kata kerja 'deny' diikuti oleh gerund (verb-ing), bukan infinitif.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Causative Verbs] -> The structure for 'have' in the causative sense is 'have + object + past participle'. 'To be repaired' is incorrect. | [Topik: Kata Kerja Kausatif] Struktur untuk 'have' dalam arti kausatif adalah 'have + objek + past participle'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Inversion with Negative Adverbials] -> When 'Not only' begins a clause, it triggers inversion. Since 'did' is the auxiliary, the main verb must be the base form 'forget'. | [Topik: Inversi dengan Kata Keterangan Negatif] Ketika 'Not only' mengawali klausa, itu memicu inversi. Kata kerja utama harus berupa bentuk dasar 'forget'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Inversion] -> Negative or restrictive adverbs like 'Little' at the beginning of a sentence require subject-auxiliary inversion ('did he know'). | [Topik: Inversi] Kata keterangan negatif atau restriktif seperti 'Little' di awal kalimat memerlukan inversi subjek-auksiliaris.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Subjunctive in Conditionals] -> In formal second conditional sentences, 'were' is used for all subjects, including 'I', 'he', 'she', and 'it'. 'Was' is considered informal or incorrect in this structure. | [Topik: Subjungtif dalam Kalimat Pengandaian] Dalam kalimat pengandaian tipe kedua yang formal, 'were' digunakan untuk semua subjek.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Absolute Phrases vs. Comma Splices] -> 'The weather was fine, we decided...' is a comma splice. Changing 'was' to 'being' creates a correct absolute phrase modifying the main clause. | [Topik: Frasa Absolut vs Comma Splice] Menggabungkan dua klausa independen dengan koma adalah kesalahan. Mengubah 'was' menjadi 'being' menciptakan frasa absolut yang benar.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Reduced Relative Clauses] -> When reducing a passive relative clause ('which are displayed'), use the past participle ('displayed'). 'Displaying' implies the artifacts are doing the action. | [Topik: Klausa Relatif yang Disederhanakan] Saat menyederhanakan klausa relatif pasif, gunakan past participle ('displayed').

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Inversion with 'Hardly'] -> The structure is 'Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when + subject + past simple'. 'Has started' is the wrong tense; it must be simple past 'started'. | [Topik: Inversi dengan 'Hardly'] Strukturnya adalah 'Hardly + had + subjek + past participle + when + subjek + past simple'.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Adjective + Preposition Collocations] -> The adjective 'capable' is followed by the preposition 'of' and a gerund ('handling'), not an infinitive. | [Topik: Kolokasi Kata Sifat + Preposisi] Kata sifat 'capable' diikuti oleh preposisi 'of' dan gerund ('handling'), bukan infinitif.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word, phrase or clause and type the correct one, or choose <no_error> and type '<no_error>'
questions.explanation: [Topic: Correlative Time Conjunctions] -> 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' are paired with 'when' (e.g., Scarcely had we... when...). 'No sooner' is paired with 'than'. | [Topik: Konjungsi Waktu Korelatif] 'Scarcely' dan 'Hardly' dipasangkan dengan 'when'. 'No sooner' dipasangkan dengan 'than'.
